title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Mechanics — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act at a point at right angles to each other. Find the magnitude and direction of their resultant.
questions.solution:
For perpendicular forces, R = √(P² + Q²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = **10 N**.

Direction: tan α = Q/P = 8/6 = 1.333, so α = **53.1° from the 6 N force** (equivalently 36.9° from the 8 N force).
questions.knowledgeNote: 6-8-10 is a scaled 3-4-5 triangle — spotting Pythagorean triples saves time in NEB numericals.

questions.question: Prove that the horizontal range of a projectile is maximum when it is projected at 45° to the horizontal.
questions.solution:
Range R = u² sin 2θ / g, where u is the projection velocity and θ the angle.

For fixed u and g, R is maximum when sin 2θ is maximum, i.e. sin 2θ = 1 → 2θ = 90° → **θ = 45°**.

The maximum range is R_max = u²/g.
questions.knowledgeNote: Complementary angles (e.g. 30° and 60°) give the same range — a favourite NEB MCQ twist.

questions.question: A block just begins to slide down a rough incline when the angle of inclination is 30°. Calculate the coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane.
questions.solution:
At the point of sliding, the angle equals the angle of repose, and μs = tan λ.

μs = tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ **0.577**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Angle of repose λ satisfies tan λ = μs — no mass term appears, so the result is independent of the block's weight.

questions.question: A pump lifts 200 kg of water per minute to a height of 10 m. Calculate the power of the pump. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
Work done per minute: W = mgh = 200 × 10 × 10 = 20,000 J.

Power P = W/t = 20,000/60 ≈ **333.3 W**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Pump/engine problems are always P = mgh/t when lifting steadily — watch whether the mass is per second or per minute.

questions.question: A gun of mass 5 kg fires a bullet of mass 10 g with a velocity of 400 m/s. Calculate the recoil velocity of the gun.
questions.solution:
By conservation of linear momentum (initial momentum zero):

M·V + m·v = 0 → V = −mv/M = −(0.01 × 400)/5 = **−0.8 m/s**.

The gun recoils at 0.8 m/s opposite to the bullet's direction.
questions.knowledgeNote: Recoil, firing, and explosion problems all start from Σp_initial = Σp_final — convert grams to kilograms first.

questions.question: A boat can move at 4 m/s in still water. It crosses a 200 m wide river with a current of 3 m/s flowing downstream. If the boat heads straight across, find (i) the crossing time and (ii) how far downstream it lands.
questions.solution:
(i) Crossing is governed only by the perpendicular component: t = width/v = 200/4 = **50 s**.

(ii) In that time the current carries it downstream by d = u·t = 3 × 50 = **150 m**.

(The boat's resultant path makes tan⁻¹(3/4) = 36.9° with the straight-across line.)
questions.knowledgeNote: Perpendicular motions are independent — the current never changes the crossing time, only the landing point.
